questions.stem:
Consider the following statements on administration and management:

1. The term 'administration' is more commonly used in government and non-profit bodies, while 'management' is more common in business enterprises
2. In the British view (E.F.L. Brech), administration is the wider term and management is only a part of it

questions.stem:

| B. Chester Barnard | 2. Structure depends on production technology (contingency view) |
| C. Joan Woodward | 3. Ideal-type bureaucracy based on rational-legal authority |
| D. Mary Parker Follett | 4. Acceptance theory of authority |

With reference to Katz's three-skill approach, consider:

1. Katz later argued that at the very top, conceptual skill can compensate for a lack of technical skill
2. Technical skill is most important for first-line supervisors who directly guide operative work
3. Conceptual skill can be dispensed with at the supervisory level since it is exercised only by the board
4. Human skill is required at all levels because every manager works with and through people

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

steps: Statement 1: correct — his 1974 retrospective noted top executives can manage with limited technical skill if conceptual/human skills are strong.
Statement 2: correct — technical proficiency needed to instruct and check work.
